<p>A standard login in OASYS is designed:
A standard login in OASYS is designed to connect users directly to specific tests. This type of login can have one or more passwords, each of which is linked to one or more tests. When a user logs in with a standard login, they are immediately connected to the tests associated with their credentials.

This setup is ideal for situations where users need direct access to specific tests without additional navigation.
<p>A student login in OASYS is specifica: A student login in OASYS is specifically designed to provide students with access to their personalized user dashboard. Unlike standard logins, which may connect users directly to specific tests, a student login directs the student to a dashboard where they can access all their available and active tests.
<p>A test taker template in OASYS is a r:
A test taker template in OASYS is a reusable login that can be connected to one or more passwords and linked to one or more tests. Each time a user logs in with a template, OASYS stores the recorded dataset as a hidden clone linked back to the template.

The datasets are listed on the template itself, so results can be tracked without filling the file manager with cloned test takers.
<p>The <b>Active Front-End Logins</b> wi:
The Active Front-End Logins widget shows tests with participants online when you can read at least one associated test taker. A test may therefore appear even if you cannot access the test itself. Switch to your Watchlist to narrow the selection.

Update mode: Manual refresh updates only when clicked, while Live auto-refresh updates automatically at short intervals when the widget is visible.

  • Active – Number of participants currently online.
  • Avg % – Average progress of all active participants (0–100%).
  • p50 % – Median progress (50th percentile).
  • p90 % – 90th percentile progress (top 10% above this value).
  • Min–Max % – Lowest and highest progress among active participants.
  • Last contact – Most recent heartbeat or activity time.

Note: Percentages are based only on currently active sessions.
<p>The Last Edited widget shows your rec:
The Last Edited widget shows your recent work history in OASYS — up to your last ten edited items (tests and page groups). It’s a quick way to pick up where you left off and to see if anything has changed since your last edit.

Visual cues help you assess the state of each entry at a glance: a red badge indicates that someone else has edited the item after you; a blocked icon means your access has been revoked.
<p>The Latest Results widget shows tests:
The Latest Results widget shows tests you can access and highlights where new results have arrived since your last login. Switch between your Watchlist and all available tests to focus on what matters most.

The “New” indicator shows how many results were added after your previous session. From here you can open the detailed results view for a test or preview a compact statistics overview.
<p>The Watchlist is your personal quick-:
The Watchlist is your personal quick-access area in the OASYS back end. Add the items you use most – tests, page groups and test takers – so you can return to them instantly without searching.

The Watchlist also performs quick checks on saved items and highlights potential issues, helping you spot problems early. You can open entries from here or remove them at any time; removing an entry only clears it from your Watchlist and does not affect the underlying content.
<p>When logging in as a student, there a:
When logging in as a student, there are three available authentication methods:

  • Direct Password: A password is set here within the OASYS system. Students will use this password to log in directly.
  • SAML: This method uses SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) authentication. It's typically used for single sign-on (SSO) across different systems. The student’s identity is authenticated by an external identity provider.
  • LDAP: LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) is used for authentication via an LDAP directory. This method allows students to log in using their LDAP credentials, which are usually managed by an organization's central directory.

Please select the appropriate authentication method for your institution's needs.
